status.scope: Fixed historical-extension design; new development comparisons executed only on existing 2013–2015 archive; 2022 evaluation not run

interpretation.main_contribution: Goal, initial coded-domain coverage, available supply and novelty-floor binding determine the interpretation and comparison needed for finite patent screening
interpretation.unit: organization-task-year screening situation, with recurrent patent selections explicitly dependent
interpretation.outcome_scope: Archival future grant links and document exposure; not engineering performance, adoption or organizational attention measured in time
interpretation.temporal_identity: A historical extension plan specified in 2026 before new-source access; not a forecast protocol made in 2022
interpretation.development_disclosure: This theoretical revision follows already examined 2018–2021 and electronics outcomes; the newly executed 2013–2015 contrasts are exploratory development analyses, not independent confirmation.

propositions.origin_condition: C0 <= 5; increasing coded-core allocation, feasible supply
propositions.mechanical: C > C0 increases coded-core seats; combined gain equals coverage gain plus within-coverage residual by identity
propositions.empirical_prediction: Coverage expansion increases mean future task-linked yield, and an equal-coverage score control reproduces more of the combined increment than changing unfamiliar selection at the same coverage
propositions.refutation: Coverage expansion has zero/negative yield, or a competitive task baseline removes the undercoverage, or within-coverage novelty consistently supplies the larger gain

propositions.mechanical: C < C0 removes C0-C coded-core seats. This concerns the domain allocation, not a low novelty floor
propositions.empirical_prediction: Mean task-linked yield falls when exiting core yield exceeds entering noncore yield
propositions.refutation: Entering noncore links compensate or exceed removed core links, or loss is confined to a weak ranker

propositions.origin_condition: Same C and noncore IDs; m is absolute minimum novel-core count
propositions.mechanical: If B(C) already has >=m novel-core candidates, selected IDs are identical under deterministic ordering; feasible binding requires a changed set and increased novel-core count
propositions.empirical_question: In binding cells, how large and uncertain are changes in total task links and novel-core-linked composition?
propositions.no_automatic_inference: More unrecorded combinations does not establish task-linked yield gain; a zero-containing interval does not establish zero effect
